id_document.description: The lab's identity-like demo card with named holder, portrait and membership identifier. This synthetic membership card is used only to demonstrate ID field extraction, not government-ID authenticity. Exclude unrelated invoice, tax and repair documents.

tax_1099a.description: An IRS Form 1099-A Acquisition or Abandonment of Secured Property, including fictional borrower-copy examples. Exclude other tax forms and prose references.

repair_estimate.description: A standalone repair workshop estimate or quote with vehicle details and proposed parts/labor. Group continuation pages of the same estimate; split a different estimate even if adjacent. Exclude towing/rental/glass invoices and their supporting inspection supplements even when they mention a proposed repair schedule.

towing_invoice.description: A towing or roadside-recovery invoice, bill or charge ledger for vehicle transport, storage or release. Keep continuation and release/custody supplements from the same bill together. Payment may be unpaid or pending; do not infer payment. Exclude repair estimates, rental agreements/billing, and glass or panel service quotes.

rental_invoice.description: A vehicle rental billing document or invoice with rental agreement references, rental dates or daily charges. Keep the same agreement's pickup/billing/vehicle-condition continuation pages together. Payment may be unpaid or pending; do not infer payment. Exclude towing bills, repair estimates, and glass or panel service quotes.

other.description: Each distinct unrouted supporting document: policy declarations/endorsements, claim intake forms, incident reports, glass/panel service supporting records, valuation/downtime schedules, and workshop inspection records. Towing bills and rental billing belong to their named invoice categories, not Other. Identify logical document boundaries even when adjacent documents both have category other. Keep paginated continuation pages together; do not merge different titles or document identifiers. These documents are intentionally unrouted, not discarded. Personal handwritten or email accounts belong to statement, not Other.

statement.description: A first-person handwritten, signed or email narrative from the claimant or vehicle owner describing the incident, discovery, circumstances or reported damage. May be a personal letter without a printed form title. Keep continuation pages of the same statement together. Exclude police/incident reports, claim intake forms, workshop estimates, invoices and policy documents. Do not infer liability or coverage.

claimant_name.description: Name explicitly identifying the claimant or insured vehicle owner. A signed first-person claimant statement may identify its author. Do not substitute the other driver, witness, adjuster or recipient. Leave absent if unclear.

incident_date.description: Date of the reported incident, not the date the email or statement was written. Leave absent if not stated.

incident_location.description: Reported incident location, using only the document text.

vehicle.description: The claimant's vehicle as explicitly stated, including year, make, model and trim when present. Exclude color and the other party's vehicle. Do not decode a VIN or infer missing details.

vin.description: Exact explicitly stated VIN of the claimant's vehicle. Do not infer, correct or substitute a plate, policy number or the other driver's VIN. Leave absent if not stated.

reported_damage.description: Damage reported to the claimant's vehicle. Attribute it as reported, not independently verified. Leave absent if not stated.

summary.description: Concise summary of the writer's reported sequence of events, including any explicit uncertainty. Do not infer fault, coverage, credibility, injuries or facts not in the source.
